```{r}
final16_17$winner <- ifelse(final16_17$Goals_Home > final16_17$Goals_Visitor, 
                           final16_17$Home_name,  # Home team wins
                           ifelse(final16_17$Goals_Home < final16_17$Goals_Visitor, 
                                  final16_17$Visitor_Name,  # Away team wins
                                  "Tie"))  # Tie case

# Print the updated dataframe
# print(final16_17)

```

```{r}
final16_17 <- final16_17 %>%
  mutate(
    Home_Won = ifelse(winner == Home_name, 1, 0),
    Away_Won = ifelse(winner == Visitor_Name, 1, 0)
  )

## 1 - yes
## 0 - no 
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

  theme_minimal()

```

  geom_boxplot() +

```{r}
# Calculate the average travel distance
avg_travel_distance <- mean(team_travel$total_distance)

# Create a new column indicating above or below average
team_travel <- team_travel %>%
  mutate(above_average = ifelse(total_distance > avg_travel_distance, "Above", "Below"))

# Calculate the proportion of teams in each conference with above-average travel
prop_table <- table(team_travel$conference, team_travel$above_average) / 
  rowSums(table(team_travel$conference, team_travel$above_average))

prop_table

```
```{r}
# ANOVA to compare travel distance across multiple conferences
aov_result <- aov(total_distance ~ conference, data = team_travel)
summary(aov_result)

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Filter for Eastern Conference teams and their divisions
eastern_divisions <- team_travel %>%
  filter(conference == "Eastern") %>%
  group_by(team, division) %>%
  summarise(total_wins = sum(wins, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(division, total_wins)

# Create the plot
ggplot(eastern_divisions, aes(x = reorder(team, total_wins), y = total_wins, fill = division)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(title = "Comparison of Wins within the Eastern Conference Divisions",
       x = "Team", 
       y = "Total Wins") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Atlantic" = "skyblue", "Metropolitan" = "lightgreen")) +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
# Filter for Western Conference teams and their divisions
western_divisions <- team_travel %>%
  filter(conference == "Western") %>%
  group_by(team, division) %>%
  summarise(total_wins = sum(wins, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(division, total_wins)

# Create the plot
ggplot(western_divisions, aes(x = reorder(team, total_wins), y = total_wins, fill = division)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(title = "Comparison of Wins within the Western Conference Divisions",
       x = "Team", 
       y = "Total Wins") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Central" = "lightcoral", "Pacific" = "lightblue")) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}

  labs(title = "Goals vs Time Zone Difference", x = "Time Zone Difference", y = "Goals") +

```

```{r}
ggplot(total_long, aes(x = as.factor(win_flag), y = Distance, fill = as.factor(win_flag))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Travel Distance vs Game Outcome", x = "Win (1) / Loss (0)", y = "Travel Distance") +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
#T-test: Do home and away teams score different amounts of goals?
t.test(Goals ~ team_type, data = total_long)
#statistically significant that home teams score more on average
#they score an avg 0.19 to 0.39 more goals
```

```{r}
# T-test: Do teams that win have more rest (days since last game)?
t.test(Days_Gap ~ win_flag, data = total_long)
#not significant
#There’s no strong evidence that rest days significantly affect winning. The slight increase in rest for winning teams is too small and not statistically significant (p = 0.097).
```

```{r}
# T-test: Do teams that win travel less?
t.test(Distance ~ win_flag, data = total_long)
#not significant
#No strong evidence that the amount of travel affects whether a team wins or loses. The difference in travel distance is small (~25 miles), and the test result (p = 0.145) suggests it's not meaningful.
```

```{r}
# Correlation: Travel distance vs goals scored
cor.test(total_long$Distance, total_long$Goals)
#No significant correlation between travel distance and goals scored. The very small negative correlation (-0.02) is essentially negligible and the p-value (0.2026) shows that this relationship is not statistically significant.
```

```{r}
#Correlation: Days of rest vs goals
cor.test(total_long$Days_Gap, total_long$Goals)
#There is a weak positive correlation between the number of rest days (Days_Gap) and the goals scored in the game (Goals). Teams that have more rest days tend to score a little more, with a statistically significant result (p = 0.0073).
```

```{r}
#Logistic Regression: Predict Win based on travel, rest, time zones
glm_model <- glm(win_flag ~ Distance + TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff + Days_Gap,
                 data = total_long, family = "binomial")
summary(glm_model)

#Distance has a statistically significant negative impact on the odds of winning. As teams travel further, their chances of winning decrease.

#Time zone difference (TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff) and Days Gap (rest days) are marginally significant. These factors seem to have some effect on the likelihood #of winning, but the evidence isn't strong enough to conclusively say they're impactful.

#The model overall suggests that rest days and travel distance could be influencing game outcomes, though there’s room for improvement in model fit (based on AIC and deviance).
```

```{r}
#ANOVA: Are average goals different across divisions?
anova_goals_div <- aov(Goals ~ Division, data = total_long)
summary(anova_goals_div)
#statistically significant difference in the mean of goals  between the different divisions in the NHL
```
```{r}
library(dplyr)

win_rate <- total_long %>%
  group_by(TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff) %>%
  summarize(win_rate = mean(win_flag, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot(win_rate, aes(x = as.factor(TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff), y = win_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Time Zone Difference",
    y = "Win Rate",
    title = "Win Rate by Time Zone Difference"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
ggplot(total_long, aes(x = Distance, y = TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "purple") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkred", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance Traveled",
    y = "Time Zone Difference",
    title = "Distance vs. Time Zone Difference"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# Remove rows with NA in relevant columns before plotting
clean_data <- total_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff), !is.na(win_flag), !is.na(Days_Gap))

ggplot(clean_data, aes(x = as.factor(TZ_Gm_to_Gm_Diff), y = win_flag, fill = as.factor(Days_Gap))) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar", position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    x = "Time Zone Difference",
    y = "Win Rate",
    fill = "Days Since Last Game",
    title = "Win Rate by Time Zone Difference and Rest Days"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
